gloss: anmitsu; Japanese dessert with red bean paste, agar jelly, and fruit

definitions.gloss: anmitsu; Japanese dessert with red bean paste, agar jelly, and fruit
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese cold dessert consisting of cubes of agar jelly ({寒天|かんてん}), sweet red bean paste ({餡|あん}), fruit pieces, mochi balls, and a sweet syrup. Served in a bowl, typically at Japanese-style tea houses and dessert shops.

examples.japanese: あんみつを{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
{夏|なつ}はあんみつがおいしい{季節|きせつ}だ。
examples.english: Summer is the season when anmitsu is at its best.

examples.japanese: {浅草|あさくさ}の{甘味処|かんみどころ}で{食|た}べたあんみつは{絶品|ぜっぴん}だった。
examples.english: The anmitsu I had at a sweets shop in Asakusa was exquisite.

notes:
A classic Japanese dessert combining {寒天|かんてん} (agar jelly) cubes, {餡|あん} (sweet red bean paste), fruit, {求肥|ぎゅうひ} (soft mochi), and {黒蜜|くろみつ} (brown sugar syrup) or other sweet syrups. The name comes from {餡|あん} (bean paste) + {蜜|みつ} (syrup/honey).

VARIATIONS:
- クリームあんみつ: anmitsu topped with ice cream or whipped cream
- {白玉|しらたま}あんみつ: anmitsu with shiratama dango (rice flour dumplings)
- {抹茶|まっちゃ}あんみつ: anmitsu with matcha-flavored elements

CULTURAL NOTE:
Anmitsu is a quintessential summer dessert in Japan, strongly associated with {甘味処|かんみどころ} (traditional Japanese sweets shops). It originated in the early 20th century as a variation of みつ{豆|まめ} (mitsumame), which is the same dessert without the bean paste.

RELATED TERMS:
- みつ{豆|まめ}: similar dessert without red bean paste
- {甘味処|かんみどころ}: traditional Japanese sweets shop
